newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU oil stocks still offer some hope for gasoline.
newsitem.headline: EU oil stocks still offer some hope for gasoline.

text.p: European Union oil stocks in March still offered some encouragement for the gasoline market despite a lower than normal drawdown, but they marked the end of a very poor distillate season, analysts said on Wednesday.
Gasoline inventories dipped by 1.23 million barrels, or 0.7 percent, in March to 164.82 million barrels.
The draw was actually smaller than is normal for the time of year, but the stocks were still 5.60 million barrels, or 3.3 percent, lower than a year ago.

"It's true to say that (the draw) is below normal. (Gasoline) is not as tight as a month ago, although of course for the market the situation is more critical now," said Geoff Pyne, oil analyst at bank UBS.
"Taking Europe as a vacuum, the (gasoline) numbers are reasonably comfortable," said Peter Bogin of oil consultants Cambridge Energy Research Associates.
However, the problem European refiners face, as all analysts pointed out, is that they rely on U.S. demand to draw away the habitual oversupply of the product.
In March, there were few problems shipping product across the Atlantic, but analysts were divided as to how long this could continue.

Some said that the return of U.S. refiners from maintenance and the resulting higher runs will leave few opportunities to export to the U.S. East Coast. Others said renewed maintenance and signs of fairly buoyant U.S. demand will continue to support European gasoline.
"There is at least another heavy period (of maintenance) in May. The peak will only come off then," said an economist with one European refiner.
The rise of crude oil stocks suggests margins, at least for gasoline production, should not come under too much strain, they said.

The crude oil build was no surprise. Crude oil stocks were up 5.99 million barrels, or 1.5 percent, in March to 397.49 million barrels, as refinery crude intake fell by 870,000 barrels per day. Crude stocks were 1.46 million barrels, or 0.4 percent, higher than year-ago levels.
The middle distillate market, meanwhile, which barely caught light this winter, is now truly consigned to the backburner.

In March, distillate stocks rose by 70,000 barrels, negligible in percentage terms, to 302.70 million barrels. The month traditionally registers a distillate draw, so the underlying surplus grew. At the end of last month, the stocks were 32.98 million barrels, or 12.2 percent, higher than a year ago.
"The stocks are very, very negative for distillates. By not coming down (in March), they are way, way up (year-on-year)," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore.
Crude and oil product stocks combined rose by 2.28 million barrels, or 0.2 percent, to 1.028 billion barrels at the end of March, largely because of the rise of crude levels.
